correctness.rationale: I reconstructed the Frobenius-orthonormal Hermitian basis, four-sample real Fourier decomposition, DC 2×3 block, paired first harmonics and 2×2 Nyquist block. The DC singular values U and 2(a²-c²), two copies each of 2b(a+c) and 2b(a-c), and the angular pair 2sqrt2 ac sqrt(1±|cos2η|) exhaust the eight outputs. The diagonal kernel diag(b²,-(a²+c²),b²) is nonzero; the smaller Nyquist singular value vanishes precisely when sin(2η)=0. Direct comparison gives largest U, smallest min(L,T sqrt(1-|cos2η|)), the unique quarter-grid optimum or full plateau, and blow-up U/(4ac|η-η0|) near resonance. I constructed full 8×9 lifting rows independently and compared SVDs in two full-rank parameter sets and one aligned rank-seven set with errors below 9e-16. This is linear lifting on quotient, not nonlinear pure-state stability.

evidence: Generic complex phase-retrieval injectivity threshold is 4d-4, eight when d=3; the current operator has a one-dimensional Hermitian kernel and rank eight in the generic stagger regime.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Generic injectivity of pure states does not calculate quotient Hermitian-lifting singular values or select a best angle. Infinite-bin Gaussian uniqueness also does not dominate finite quantitative conditioning.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Quantitative conditioning requires the DC/first-harmonic/Nyquist block spectral calculation and the piecewise minimax; it is not a corollary of known generic counts of magnitude samples.

evidence: Liu-Ning-Wu-Zhang 2026 use Gaussian two-bin sampled magnitudes for Paley-Wiener L² uniqueness; Wellershoff 2022 gives two-bin Gabor magnitude uniqueness.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Those stated prior theorems address infinite L² signals and uniqueness of phaseless sampling; the object here is the finite three-atomic Hermitian 8×9 lifting and its exact singular values. The stronger statement of exact conditioning is not implied by uniqueness alone.
